title: The Saturday Night Massacre, 1973 — two men who resigned rather than obey
sources: Wikipedia: Saturday Night Massacre — on Saturday 20 October 1973, Nixon ordered Attorney General Elliot Richardson to fire special prosecutor Archibald Cox, who was investigating Watergate and had refused to drop a subpoena for the White House tapes; Richardson refused and resigned; Deputy Attorney General William Ruckelshaus also refused and resigned; Solicitor General Robert Bork carried out the dismissal (he said he intended to resign afterwards but was persuaded to stay); public opinion turned against Nixon; the impeachment process began ten days later, on 30 October; Nixon resigned 9 months and 20 days later, on 9 August 1974
Also on this day (candidates.md, in the app): 1973 Elizabeth II opens the Sydney Opera House after 14 years of construction; 1740 Maria Theresa ascends the Habsburg throne

Photos (public domain, US government / Library of Congress / NARA): Richard Nixon; Nixon with his Cabinet, 1972; Archibald Cox, June 1973 and 20 October 1973; Elliot Richardson; William Ruckelshaus sworn in as EPA administrator; Robert Bork; the Watergate complex
Illustrative stock footage (Pexels, free licence; not of the event): a rotary telephone, a typewriter

post.facebook:
On the night of Saturday 20 October 1973, Richard Nixon tried to stop the Watergate investigation — and lost two of his top law officers in the process.

Special prosecutor Archibald Cox had refused to drop his subpoena for the tapes Nixon had secretly recorded in the White House. Nixon ordered Attorney General Elliot Richardson to fire him. Richardson refused, and resigned. Nixon gave the same order to Deputy Attorney General William Ruckelshaus. He refused too, and resigned. The third man in line, Solicitor General Robert Bork, carried it out.

The country called it the Saturday Night Massacre. Public opinion turned sharply against the president; ten days later the impeachment process began. On 9 August 1974, Nixon resigned.

Also on 20 October: the Sydney Opera House opened after 14 years of construction (1973), and Maria Theresa took the Habsburg throne (1740).

youtube.description:
20 October 1973 — the Saturday Night Massacre. Nixon ordered Attorney General Elliot Richardson to fire Watergate special prosecutor Archibald Cox, who wanted the secret White House tapes. Richardson refused and resigned. Deputy William Ruckelshaus refused and resigned. The third in line, Robert Bork, carried out the order. Ten days later the impeachment process began; less than ten months later, Nixon resigned.

Also on 20 October: the Sydney Opera House opens (1973) and Maria Theresa takes the Habsburg throne (1740).
